_provenance.status: APP-AUTHORED catalogue — the notification service has no contract and nothing has been sent (see lib/api-client/notifications.ts)
brief: Captain checklist (2026-09-19): the Notifications screen (/staff/notifications) was a twelve-line stub; it is now the messages the product will send, to whom and through which channel, with the recorded sent log.

The catalogue follows the blueprint's own notification engine (docs/04-modules/documents-contracts.md §Notifications, blueprint §41): channels email · SMS · Messenger/approved messaging · push · in-app; events payment due · reservation expiry · viewing · interment · appointment · document status · operational alerts; template management + event-driven rules, configurable per tenant.
note: WHAT THIS IS: the four notification types the product is designed to send (booking confirmation · payment reminder · document-ready note · service reminder), each with its trigger, audience and channel — described, not configured. The platform's notification service is P4 (docs/02-architecture/microservices.md:39) and does not exist in this build: `service_state` is `not_wired` and the service exposes no outward API, so live mode is not a thing that can be switched on here.

THE LOG IS EMPTY ON PURPOSE: nothing has been sent, and no placeholder message may be fabricated to make the screen look alive — the family notifications page takes the same line (`app/(family)/client/notifications/page.tsx`). A real entry arrives only when the notification service records one.

WHAT THE SCREEN ADDS: the four things the service must settle before this page can list a delivery — template management, event rules, per-tenant configuration and consent (`docs/02-architecture/microservices.md:98`, blueprint §41 'lawful marketing only with consent').

No template body, no send schedule and no recipient detail appears anywhere in this file; the vocabulary (audiences, channels, log states) lives in lib/notifications.ts and is pinned by tests/fixture-contract/notifications.test.ts.
